reasons: Compliant claim is supported by the cited text: Section 15.9 selects Delaware law, which is expressly within the playbook fallback (Delaware or California), and the rationale correctly states it sits at the fallback rather than the preferred New York position.

No walk-away trigger is present: the arbitral seat is New York (15.10.2.2), so there is no foreign law, foreign venue, or arbitration seated abroad; IP ownership/validity disputes are reserved to a U.S. federal court and either Party may seek injunctive relief in any competent court.

Consistent with playbook classification semantics, no redline or counterparty comment is proposed for a fallback-compliant clause; the shortfalls (Delaware vs. New York law, domestic arbitration vs. New York County courts) are appropriately noted in the rationale rather than flagged as deviations. Deterministic check on accepted governing law passes and the redline is identical to the original text.

Minor accuracy nit (non-material): the rationale attributes a U.S. Federal Arbitration Act reference to 15.10.2.2, which is not visible in the quoted paragraph; the seat-in-New-York language alone supports the conclusion.
